title: Organizing jQuery Code
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of organizing jquery code in a jQuery application.
Apply separating behavior from presentation in a small example and describe its expected result.
Verify dividing code into reusable functions with an explicit test or browser observation.
status_note: Draft generated from the attached syllabus and official references; requires lesson-by-lesson technical review, local execution, accessibility checks, and editorial approval.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through organizing jquery code with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns separating behavior from presentation into a repeatable implementation choice. Use small functions, scoped state, explicit initialization, and cleanup to prevent global namespace pollution and duplicate event handlers.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Use small functions, scoped state, explicit initialization, and cleanup to prevent global namespace pollution and duplicate event handlers.

content_blocks.expected_output: A small helper updates text and state class in one place.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Use a local HTML page with jQuery 4.0.0 loaded before app.js for JavaScript snippets. HTML and package-manager snippets can be checked as configuration examples. Run the interaction in browser DevTools, inspect the DOM/Network panel, and compare actual behavior with the expected result. Do not submit learner code to the production API for arbitrary execution.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original markup and code, clear console/network filters, reload the local page, and repeat the same interaction. For a request example, return the mock endpoint to its original response before retrying.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with a known DOM structure, apply the pattern for organizing jquery code, and test one normal case plus one edge case. Keep selectors scoped to the intended component and verify the real browser result.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Refactor an existing snippet around organizing jquery code into a named function with explicit inputs. Mount it twice and prove that repeated setup does not duplicate behavior.

content.task: Refactor an existing snippet around organizing jquery code into a named function with explicit inputs. Mount it twice and prove that repeated setup does not duplicate behavior.
task_acceptance_criteria: The implementation demonstrates organizing jquery code using a current, documented approach.
The learner records the expected and actual behavior and checks at least one edge case.
The example preserves semantic HTML and does not render untrusted data as HTML.
The test setup and any runtime limitation are documented honestly.
hints: First identify which DOM nodes and runtime state are involved in organizing jquery code.
Make one small change, inspect the resulting element or request, and compare it with the expected result.
If the result differs, check the selector, script order, browser console, event target, and relevant API documentation before adding more code.
content.expected_output: A small helper updates text and state class in one place.
common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
summary: Organizing jQuery Code is one part of the code organization and reusable patterns workflow.
Use small functions, scoped state, explicit initialization, and cleanup to prevent global namespace pollution and duplicate event handlers.
Use the official API or upgrade guide for version-specific behavior and verify an example locally before relying on it.
